items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: And you'll be here tomorrow night at the Dawson's Band. And after that, well, he, the next day, Harry Parker went and got a permit for the trumpet. And he worked there with us then from that on.

ctx.x: Yeah, I know F.S. He played there

Yeah, yeah, I know Neal Lavish there He played, you know, he was a violin player Oh, he violin That was his band Yeah, it was his band And that fella Few Clothes had his dance hall there And then the next block from there Was Harry Park and Charlie Park Called 101 Ranch And that's where I played there
That must have been around 1907. Harry Parker's dance hall, that's a... Was that the 101 Ranch? 101 Ranch, me and Manetta. Mani Manetta.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: He played violin with me over there. They, uh, uh, they fired, uh, one time they, uh, they had gotten a humbug. He'd gotten a humbug with a woman around there in the place. Uh, Jim Palau laid off. I think he laid off from there one night. And he sent a tinette in his place. ... Parker the boss man c

ctx.x: They used to have your small band. Yeah.

Uh, well, you see, uh, they used to dance. They had, uh, they sell liquor there, you know, they had women working there, uh, hustling. And, uh, the fellas, people would come in there. Most of the men from off the ships, they'd come in there and spend money and dance. And go on and have a good time and put, uh, we had a kiddie box that we, that dropped the money in the kiddie box for the different numbers that they want to hear, you see. And, uh, now, uh, T-Net played, uh, the last I heard of him, he played with…

What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: Harry Parker asked me what instrument was that... he asked me, do you think you can get that fella to play a regular? ... We started around by Harry Parker. And yes, Harry Parker, that's when we started that Dixieland.

ctx.x: It was against the law, was it?

It was against the law to blow brass instruments in the district. So, uh, Harry Parker asked me what instrument was that and I told him a trumpet. So he said, well tell him to play something. And he said, oh boss I can't play nothing, it's a violation of the law. I'm afraid, but if you protect me, I'll play. He said, well I'll, I'll protect you. He said, go ahead, there ain't nobody gonna do you nothing. So he blowed his trumpet and right after that he asked, it sounds so good he asked me, do you think you can…
Previously that was all string band.
